rule: Keep the first (partition) dimension of every SBUF and PSUM tensor at or below 128.
why: SBUF has 128 physical partitions; dim 0 of an on-chip tensor maps one-to-one onto them, so a larger dim 0 cannot be allocated.

why: On gen2/gen3 a matmul result must fit one PSUM bank (512 fp32 elements); on gen4 the destination may span all of PSUM: 4096 fp32 or 8192 bf16 elements. psum_bank_fmax is a fixed 512 and is not dtype- or generation-aware.
trigger: Any PSUM allocation or nc_matmul/nc_transpose dst whose free dim exceeds the limit, or code that hardcodes PSUM_FREE_MAX = 512 on gen4 (under-tiles) or branches on nc_version.
fix: Tile N to 512 on trn1/trn2; on trn3 use up to 4096 (fp32 dst) / 8192 (bf16 dst); confirm against the nc_matmul doc block.

rule: Treat a PSUM bank as 2 KiB per partition (512 fp32) and place concurrent accumulations or transposes in different banks via address=(0, bank*2048) or by cycling nl.tile_size.psum_num_banks.
why: PSUM is organized as banks of 2048 bytes per partition; two in-flight matmul/transpose groups writing the same bank conflict and serialize.
trigger: Multiple nc_transpose/nc_matmul groups in flight that target overlapping PSUM addresses.
fix: Allocate psum_bank_i = nl.ndarray(..., buffer=nl.psum, address=(0, i * 2048)) and alternate banks across concurrent groups.

rule: Shape nc_matmul operands as stationary [K<=128, M<=128] and moving [K<=128, N<=nl.tile_size.gemm_moving_fmax] with the result [M, N] in PSUM.
why: The tensor engine contracts over the partition dimension of both operands; the stationary free dim is bounded by the PE array width (128) and the moving free dim by gemm_moving_fmax (512 on gen2/3).

fix: Tile M to 128, N to gemm_moving_fmax (512), K to 128 per instruction and accumulate over K tiles in PSUM.

rule: Tile nc_transpose inputs to at most 128x128 and route the output through PSUM before further use.
why: nc_transpose is executed on the tensor engine as an identity TRANSPOSE matmul using the PSUM array as intermediate buffer, so both dims are bounded by the PE array and the dst by the PSUM free-dim limit.
trigger: nc_transpose on a tile larger than 128x128 or with a PSUM dst whose free dim exceeds the PSUM limit ('PSUM dimension exceeds limit').
fix: Loop over 128x128 chunks: nisa.nc_transpose(dst=out[f:f+128, p:p+128], data=in[p:p+128, f:f+128]); then nisa.tensor_copy PSUM->SBUF.

rule: Use a PSUM step size of 2 (allocate twice the PSUM free extent) when nc_transpose operates on fp8 or int8 data.
why: 1-byte dtypes occupy PSUM at 2-byte granularity, so the transposed result is written with stride 2 in the PSUM free dimension.
trigger: nc_transpose with data dtype in {nl.float8_e4m3, nl.float8_e5m2, nl.int8} (and MX types on gen4).
fix: psum_step_size = 2 if dtype in (fp8_e4m3, fp8_e5m2, int8) else 1; size the PSUM dst and .ap() pattern stride by psum_step_size.
check_sketch: nc_transpose: if itemsize == 1 then PSUM dst extent >= 2 * logical free size

rule: Never reshape, stride, flatten, reverse, or permute the partition dimension of an SBUF/PSUM tensor through indexing or views; only contiguous slices of dim 0 are legal.
why: Dim 0 is physically distributed across 128 hardware partitions; logical rearrangement of it requires an explicit nc_transpose instruction.
trigger: tensor[::2, :], tensor[::-1, :], tensor.reshape changing dim 0, .flatten(), .T, TensorView.permute moving dim 0, reshape_dim(0,...), flatten_dims(0,...).
fix: Use tensor[a:b, :] / nl.ds(offset, size) on dim 0; use nisa.nc_transpose for P<->F swaps; reshape or permute only free dims (dim >= 1).

rule: Reduce only along free axes (axis >= 1) with nisa.tensor_reduce; never pass axis=0.
why: Vector/scalar engines reduce within a partition; there is no single instruction that reduces across partitions.
trigger: nisa.tensor_reduce(..., axis=0) or a reduction whose target dimension is the partition dimension.
fix: Reduce free dims per partition first, then move the per-partition results across partitions (nc_transpose or matmul against a ones vector) and reduce again; for 3D/4D data pass the correct axis tuple.

rule: Keep the total contraction (K) dimension handled by one accumulation group at or below 2048 and tile K beyond that.
why: The documented per-tile contraction limit for nc_matmul is 2048; larger K must be split into multiple accumulation groups.
trigger: A matmul whose K dimension exceeds 2048 elements.
fix: Split K into chunks of <= 2048 (each itself in 128-row operand tiles) and accumulate in PSUM.

rule: Keep total model tensors (I/O + internal + spills) within 32 GB HBM per device and any single output tensor under 4 GB.
why: neuronx-cc rejects NEFFs whose tensor footprint exceeds HBM (NCC_EOOM001/002, NCC_EVRF009) or whose output exceeds the 4 GB limit (NCC_EVRF024).
trigger: Compiler errors NCC_EOOM001, NCC_EOOM002, NCC_EVRF009, NCC_EXSP001, NCC_EVRF024.
fix: Reduce batch/sequence size, shard with tensor/pipeline parallelism, use bf16/fp16 instead of fp32, or split the output tensor.
check_sketch: sum(sizeof(inputs)+sizeof(outputs)) <= 32 GiB; max(sizeof(output)) < 4 GiB

rule: Keep the generated instruction count under the NEFF limit by avoiding deep full unrolling of large loops; split the kernel or use runtime loops when it is exceeded.
why: affine_range/static_range/range loops are fully unrolled at compile time, so every iteration becomes separate instructions; the compiler raises NCC_EVRF007/NCC_EBVF030/NCC_EXTP004 when the per-NEFF limit is exceeded.
trigger: Compiler error 'The number of instructions generated exceeds the limit' (NCC_EVRF007, NCC_EBVF030, NCC_EXTP004).
fix: Increase tile sizes to reduce iteration count, move hot loops to nl.fori_loop (structured on-chip loop, not unrolled), or split into multiple kernels.
check_sketch: estimate unrolled instruction count = sum(product of trip counts of nested unrolled loops * ops per body); warn above a configurable threshold

rule: Control PSUM initialization with accumulate=(k_idx > 0) on nisa.nc_matmul and never nisa.memset the PSUM tile before the K loop.
why: accumulate=False makes the first matmul overwrite (initialize) the PSUM location in hardware; a memset is a wasted instruction and accumulate=True on an uninitialized location is invalid.
trigger: nisa.memset(dst=psum, ...) preceding a matmul accumulation loop, or accumulate=True on the first K tile.
fix: psum = nl.ndarray((M,N), nl.float32, buffer=nl.psum); for k in nl.affine_range(nk): nisa.nc_matmul(dst=psum, stationary=a, moving=b, accumulate=(k > 0)).
check_sketch: flag memset whose dst.buffer == psum; flag nc_matmul with accumulate=True that is the first writer of its dst

rule: Iterate the matmul K (contraction) accumulation loop with nl.affine_range (or range), never nl.sequential_range.
why: sequential_range forces serialization and prevents the compiler from pipelining the accumulation group; affine_range lets consecutive matmuls stream back-to-back into PSUM.
trigger: for k in nl.sequential_range(...) wrapping nisa.nc_matmul with a PSUM dst.
fix: Replace with nl.affine_range(num_k_tiles) and accumulate=(k_idx > 0).
check_sketch: flag sequential_range loops whose body contains nc_matmul accumulating into the same PSUM dst

rule: Never write the PSUM accumulator to HBM (or copy it out) between K-accumulation steps.
why: Each copy-out breaks the hardware accumulation chain and adds HBM traffic; PSUM accumulation in FP32 is nearly free.
trigger: dma_copy/tensor_copy with src=psum inside the K loop.
fix: Move the PSUM->SBUF tensor_copy after the K loop completes.
check_sketch: flag reads of a PSUM accumulator inside the loop that accumulates into it

rule: Always copy PSUM results to SBUF with nisa.tensor_copy before any DMA to HBM; direct PSUM->HBM dma_copy is forbidden (NKI 0.3.0+).
why: DMA engines cannot source from PSUM; tensor_copy on the vector/scalar engine evacuates PSUM and can convert dtype in the same instruction.
trigger: nisa.dma_copy(dst=hbm, src=psum_tile).
fix: sb = nl.ndarray(psum.shape, out_dtype, buffer=nl.sbuf); nisa.tensor_copy(dst=sb, src=psum); nisa.dma_copy(dst=hbm, src=sb).
check_sketch: dma_copy: assert src.buffer != psum and dst.buffer != psum

rule: Accumulate partial matmul products in PSUM via the tensor engine rather than summing partial results on the vector engine with tensor_tensor.
why: PSUM accumulation is done in FP32 by the PE array with very low overhead; VectorE tensor_tensor accumulation is significantly slower and adds PSUM->SBUF traffic per partial.
trigger: A pattern of nc_matmul into fresh PSUM per K tile followed by tensor_tensor(op=nl.add) to combine.
fix: Reuse one PSUM dst across K tiles with accumulate=(k_idx > 0).
check_sketch: flag tensor_tensor(add) whose operands are both results of nc_matmul over disjoint K ranges

rule: Issue matmuls with full tiles K=128, M=128, N=512 (stationary [128,128], moving [128,512]) whenever the problem allows.
why: TE throughput per initiation interval scales with the tile: undersized M or K reduce throughput linearly; a (128,512) tile keeps PSUM pipelining efficient.
trigger: nc_matmul with M < 128 or K < 128 on hot source lines; profile shows K/128, M/128 < 1.
fix: Re-tile so stationary and moving operands use the full 128-partition contraction and M=128; pad or batch small dims.

rule: When something must be undersized, shrink N (moving free dim) rather than M or K.
why: The moving operand streams through the PE array, so a shorter N shortens the initiation interval proportionally; M and K underutilization leave PE rows/columns idle and cut throughput linearly.

fix: Keep K=128 and M=128; let N be whatever remains (e.g. 64) if needed.

rule: Give vector/scalar engine instructions a free dimension of at least 64 elements (prefer 128) with the full 128 partitions.
why: Each instruction has fixed issue overhead; tiny free dims make static instruction overhead dominate execution.
trigger: activation/tensor_tensor/tensor_scalar on tiles with free dim < 64.
fix: Use column_tiling_dim = 32 if T<=32, 64 if T<=64, else 128 (production mlp_tkg rule); batch rows to fill 128 partitions.
check_sketch: for vector/scalar ISA ops: warn if dst free size < 64

rule: Lay out every on-chip tile so the partition dimension is the full 128 (H0 = nl.tile_size.pmax) and fold remaining size into the free dims.
why: Each partition is an independent lane of every compute engine; using fewer partitions leaves lanes idle.
trigger: Tiles allocated with shape[0] < 128 on hot paths (e.g. a [T, ...] tile with small token count T in decode).
fix: Reshape the problem so a 128-multiple dimension (hidden/H) is on partitions: e.g. [H] -> [128, H/128]; put the small dim (T) on the free axis.
check_sketch: warn if an SBUF tile shape[0] < 128 while another dim is a multiple of 128

rule: Supply matmul operands already in [K, M] (lhsT) layout instead of transposing tiles on-device with nc_transpose.
why: nc_transpose executes as TRANSPOSE MATMUL instructions that consume tensor engine FLOPs without useful work; one transpose per matmul added 11.1% of hardware FLOPs and 24% of runtime in the worked example.
trigger: Profile gap compute_bound_ideal_flops -> compute_bound_ideal_useful_flops > 0, or Summary.transpose_flops > 0; code calls nc_transpose inside the matmul loop.
fix: Pre-transpose weights at load time (or ask for the transposed layout) and pass lhsT[K, M] directly as the stationary operand.
check_sketch: count Instruction rows with tensor_instruction_type == 'TRANSPOSE'; report transpose_flops / hw_flops per source line

numbers.example_transpose_overhead: 11.1% of hw_flops, 27.3 us at peak, 24% total time

rule: Block the output over M and N so each input tile is loaded once per block and reused across many matmuls, rather than reloading operands in the innermost loop.
why: With naive (m, n, k) loops each rhs tile is reloaded once per m-tile; blocking cut rhs reloads from 32x to 3x, reduced DMA time 6x and total time 3.5x in the worked example.
trigger: Profile excess_ratio >> 1 with reload_excess dominating; TensorInfo input repeat factor > 1.5x.
fix: Pre-load lhsT tiles for an M-block (e.g. 8-12 tiles) into SBUF, load each rhs K-tile once per (m_block, n), then run all bm x k matmuls.
check_sketch: repeat = sum(DmaPacketAggregated.transfer_bytes for IN tensor)/TensorInfo.size; flag > 1.5

rule: Load full block-width rows (e.g. [128, 1024] bf16) with one dma_copy and slice them in SBUF for matmuls, instead of one DMA per 128x128 or 128x512 tile.
why: Same bytes in fewer, larger descriptors raises achieved DMA bandwidth (151.9 -> 245.8 GB/s) and removes TE starvation gaps.
trigger: Many dma_copy calls each moving <= 1 KiB per partition; profile shows DMA inefficiency gap and TE idle spans waiting on DMA.
fix: Allocate row = nl.ndarray((128, BLOCK), ...), one dma_copy per K tile, then nc_matmul(stationary=row[:, bm*128:(bm+1)*128], ...).
check_sketch: desc_bytes = transfer_bytes / partitions per source line; flag < 2048

rule: Make the contiguous (stride-1) free dimension of every dma_copy at least 2 KiB per partition: 512 fp32, 1024 bf16, or 2048 fp8 elements.
why: DMA efficiency depends on long contiguous runs per partition; short or strided runs pay per-descriptor overhead and cannot saturate HBM bandwidth.
trigger: dma_copy whose innermost contiguous extent * itemsize < 2048 bytes, or whose innermost stride != 1.
fix: Re-tile or reshape (e.g. [HTile=2048, I] -> [128, 16, I]) so the innermost free dim is large and contiguous; use .ap(pattern=[[...],[1, I]]) with stride 1 innermost.
check_sketch: for dma_copy: innermost pattern stride == 1 and innermost size * itemsize >= 2048

rule: Aim for a DMA descriptor size (transfer_bytes / partitions) of at least 4 KiB; below that transfers are significantly less efficient and above it gains are marginal.
why: Each DMA transfer/packet has fixed overhead; throughput correlates with descriptor size until ~4 KiB, after which larger descriptors trade off against pipelining granularity.
trigger: Profile DmaPacketAggregated shape PxDB with D < 4096; achieved_bw well below dma_ddr_bandwidth.
fix: Widen the free dimension of the dma_copy (e.g. 128x512 bf16 -> 128x2048 bf16 raised achieved BW from 259 to 354 GB/s).

rule: Transfer whole tiles in one dma_copy; never loop issuing one DMA per row, element, or partition.
why: Per-DMA fixed cost dominates when payloads are tiny; 128 single-row DMAs cost far more than one [128, F] DMA.
trigger: dma_copy inside a Python/affine loop whose src/dst slice covers one partition or one element.
fix: Hoist the DMA out of the loop: nisa.dma_copy(dst=sb[0:128, :], src=hbm[0:128, :]).
check_sketch: flag dma_copy with dst shape[0] == 1 inside a loop over partitions, or total bytes < 512

rule: Load each HBM input once into SBUF and reuse the tile for all consumers; never re-DMA the same region.
why: Every redundant load adds HBM traffic that counts against memory_bound_ideal_no_reloads; HBM bandwidth is the scarcest resource in memory-bound kernels.
trigger: Two dma_copy calls with identical src slices; profile reload repeat > 1.
fix: Keep the first tile alive and pass it to both compute paths.
check_sketch: detect duplicate (src tensor, slice) pairs across dma_copy calls reachable without an intervening overwrite

fix: If possible change the HBM layout to be contiguous; otherwise accept strided DMA (gen3+) and avoid extra SBUF copies.

rule: For interleaved<->contiguous relayouts of tensors whose flattened free size fits nl.tile_size.gemm_moving_fmax, use a permutation-matrix matmul in SBUF instead of strided DMA.
why: A permutation matmul runs at TE speed on data already in SBUF; strided DMA pays HBM descriptor overhead. For larger tensors only strided DMA fits.
trigger: RoPE-style even/odd interleave with B*n_heads*S <= gemm_moving_fmax (~512).
fix: Build perm_matrix [d_head, d_head] via .ap() patterns ([[d_head,d_head],[1,2],[2,half_d]]) and compute nc_matmul(perm, x).
check_sketch: if relayout tensor free size <= gemm_moving_fmax -> suggest permutation matmul else strided DMA

rule: When the given tensor layout forces strided DMA or complex reshaping, ask the user to change it: reduction dim last (contiguous), dims aligned to 128 (partition) and 512 (PSUM free), pre-transposed to avoid strided loads.
why: Layout determines whether DMA can issue long contiguous descriptors and whether matmul tiles are full; a layout fix removes overhead no kernel-side trick can.
trigger: Input layout requires TensorView.slice(step) gathers or nc_transpose in the hot loop.
fix: Propose: 'Would you allow changing the layout to [proposed]? This simplifies the kernel and improves performance.'
check_sketch: flag kernels where >50% of DMA bytes are strided or where every matmul is preceded by nc_transpose

rule: Use no DGE for compile-time indices, dge_mode=nisa.dge_mode.swdge for small unrolled loops (< 16 iterations), and dge_mode=nisa.dge_mode.hwdge for >= 16 iterations or runtime-computed indices (fori_loop/while_loop bodies).
why: No-DGE descriptors are precomputed (lowest overhead); SWDGE generates descriptors in software per unrolled iteration (low overhead); HWDGE computes them on-chip (medium overhead but handles true runtime indices).
trigger: dma_copy with nl.ds() offsets from a loop variable or a VirtualRegister.
fix: Add dge_mode=nisa.dge_mode.swdge / hwdge per the table; never pass integer enums or engine=.
check_sketch: dma_copy with runtime (register) index must have dge_mode == hwdge; unrolled loop < 16 iters -> swdge

rule: For HBM->SBUF loads that need a transposed layout, use nisa.dma_transpose in one step rather than dma_copy followed by nc_transpose.
why: dma_transpose performs the transpose inside the DMA engine, saving tensor-engine TRANSPOSE matmuls and a PSUM round trip; note transposed DMA loads are themselves less efficient than plain loads.
trigger: dma_copy immediately followed by nc_transpose of the same tile in the load path.
fix: nisa.dma_transpose(dst=sbuf[0:p, 0:f], src=hbm[0:f, 0:p]) with dst rank exactly matching the transposed src rank (NKI 0.4.0).

rule: Give nisa.dma_transpose a dst whose shape equals the transposed src shape exactly, including rank (NKI 0.4.0).
why: The 0.4.0 compiler enforces rank equality; a 3D dst for a 4D src is a compilation failure.
trigger: dma_transpose(dst=3D, src=4D, axes=...) or any rank mismatch.
fix: Allocate dst with the permuted 4D shape, e.g. src (128,1,1,4096) with axes=(3,1,2,0) -> dst (4096,1,1,128).
check_sketch: dma_transpose: assert len(dst.shape) == len(src.shape) and dst.shape == permute(src.shape, axes)

rule: Implement scatter-add / HBM accumulation with nisa.dma_compute(dst, srcs=[...], reduce_op=nl.add, unique_indices=...) instead of dst_rmw_op or a manual load+add+store.
why: dst_rmw_op was removed in NKI 0.3.0; dma_compute performs the reduction in the DMA path, avoiding an extra SBUF round trip and serialization.

rule: Measure DMA time as the interval-merged wall-clock time across all 16 DMA engines (dma_active_time), never the sum of per-packet durations.

rule: Fold a preceding multiply and/or add into nisa.activation via scale= and bias= (exp(x*s), sigmoid(x+b), tanh(x*s+b)) instead of a separate tensor_scalar.
why: ScalarE applies a pipelined multiply-add before the nonlinear function, so two ops cost one instruction; the separate form is 2x slower.

fix: nisa.activation(dst=out, op=nl.exp, data=x, scale=s, bias=b).

rule: Implement cumsum, cumprod, RNN-style and SSM recurrences with a single nisa.tensor_tensor_scan per tile and carry the last column as initial= to the next tile, instead of a sequential loop over elements.
why: An explicit loop emits seq_len instructions each on a 1-element-per-partition tile with data dependencies, so static instruction overhead dominates; the scan instruction caches intermediates inside VectorE.

fix: nisa.tensor_tensor_scan(dst, data0, data1, initial, op0=nl.multiply, op1=nl.add) computing out[i] = op0(data0[i], out[i-1]) op1 data1[i]; cumsum uses data0=ones, cumprod uses data1=zeros, initial=1.

rule: Use nisa.reciprocal(dst, data) and nisa.rsqrt(dst, data) rather than nisa.activation(op=nl.reciprocal/nl.rsqrt).

fix: Replace with nisa.reciprocal(dst=inv, data=x) / nisa.rsqrt(dst=r, data=x).

rule: Pass nl.exp, nl.sigmoid, nl.tanh, nl.gelu etc. only as op= specifiers to nisa.activation/tensor_tensor; never call them as functions.
why: These symbols are enum-like operator specifiers; calling nl.exp(tensor) does not lower to an instruction.

fix: nisa.activation(dst=y, data=x, op=nl.exp); nisa.tensor_tensor(dst=y, data1=a, data2=b, op=nl.add).

rule: Replicate a bias/scale that lives in partition 0 to all 128 partitions with stream_shuffle_broadcast (nc_stream_shuffle); use tp_broadcast only for the rare column-vector (P) to row (F) broadcast.
why: There is no cross-partition broadcast via indexing; the stream-shuffle engine path moves a partition-0 row to every PE lane without a DMA round trip.
trigger: A 1-D parameter loaded into one partition that must be applied to every row of a [128, F] tile.
fix: stream_shuffle_broadcast(src, dst) before the tensor_tensor/activation that consumes it.

rule: Express reshapes, permutes of free dims, free-dim broadcasts (stride 0) and strided slices as zero-copy views (NkiTensor methods, TensorView, or .ap()) rather than chains of nisa.tensor_copy.
why: Views are compile-time stride computations with no runtime cost; each tensor_copy is a full vector-engine pass over the tile and consumes SBUF.

rule: Use SbufManager (stack/heap SBUF allocation) when a kernel has 4+ SBUF tensors or sub-functions sharing SBUF; plain nl.ndarray is fine for 1-3 buffers.

rule: Treat DmaPacketAggregated rows whose source/dest contains [VIRTUAL] as compiler-inserted SBUF spills and shrink the live SBUF footprint of the source line they trace to.
why: When live tiles exceed SBUF the compiler evicts to HBM and reloads; each spill costs a save plus a reload (spill_cost = 2 x reload bytes) at DMA bandwidth.
trigger: spill_bytes dominating excess traffic in the redundant-DMA investigation.
fix: Reduce tile lifetime (consume PSUM/SBUF results immediately), lower blocking factors, or use SbufManager; trace via Flow.DGE_TRIGGER to the NKI op whose output was spilled.

rule: Prefer fused ISA ops (activation_reduce, tensor_scalar_reduce, tensor_scalar_cumulative, activate2) over an elementwise op followed by a separate tensor_reduce when the pattern matches.

fix: nisa.activation_reduce(...) producing both the activated tile and the row reduction.

fix: Operate directly on the bf16 tile; convert once in the PSUM->SBUF tensor_copy if a different output dtype is needed.

rule: Run matmuls in bf16/fp16 (or fp8 on trn2+) rather than fp32: on trn2 fp32 matmul costs 4x the TE time per FLOP and fp8 costs 0.5x.
why: The profiler's adjusted_flops normalizes to bf16-equivalent FLOPs with 1x for bf16/fp16/tf32, 4x for fp32, 0.5x for fp8 on trn2, reflecting the PE array's native rates.
trigger: nc_matmul operands in nl.float32 on hot paths.
fix: Cast operands to bf16 (accumulate in fp32 PSUM); consider fp8 with per-row scaling on gen3+.

rule: Pass a memset value whose Python type matches the destination dtype (integer literal for int buffers, float for float buffers).

fix: nisa.memset(dst=int_buf, value=2); nisa.memset(dst=f32_buf, value=0.0).
check_sketch: memset: type(value) consistent with dst.dtype kind

rule: Keep all integer constants and index arithmetic within 32-bit range (int32/uint32); Neuron engines have no 64-bit datapath.
why: neuronx-cc raises NCC_ESFH002 when a 64-bit constant cannot be safely converted to 32-bit; shift-right-arithmetic requires 32-bit first operands (NCC_EVRF022).
trigger: uint64/int64 constants > 4,294,967,295 or bitwise shifts on int16 operands.
fix: Use int32/uint32; split large values into multiple 32-bit operations or precompute on CPU.
check_sketch: flag int64/uint64 literals outside int32/uint32 range in kernel code

rule: Perform scatter-reduce / dma_compute reductions on floating-point tensors; cast integer or boolean data to float first.
why: Hardware scatter-reduce instructions only implement floating-point arithmetic (NCC_EVRF016).
trigger: Reduction scatter into an int32/bool destination.
fix: Cast indices-side data to float32/bf16 before the reduce and back afterwards if needed.
check_sketch: dma_compute/scatter_reduce: assert dst.dtype and src.dtype are float

rule: Compute the reference result on CPU (tensor.cpu()) and compare with several metrics (allclose atol/rtol, max abs diff, norm of diff, cosine similarity) using dtype-appropriate tolerances.
why: Every on-device XLA graph compiles to its own NEFF, so a device-side reference pollutes profiling and NEFF identification; a single metric misses outliers or drift.
trigger: Test harness calling torch.matmul/softmax on the XLA device, or a single allclose check.
fix: expected = ref(x.cpu()); out = kernel(x).cpu(); check allclose + max|diff| + ||diff|| + cosine.
check_sketch: flag reference computations on tensors whose device is xla

fix: Insert temporary dma_copy of each stage output, binary-search the failing stage, then remove the debug stores.

trigger: print(tile) used to debug data values.
fix: nl.device_print(...) for on-device values; print() only for shapes/patterns.
check_sketch: flag print() calls whose argument is an on-chip tensor

rule: Pick loop constructs by dependency: nl.affine_range for independent iterations (full unroll, schedulable), nl.sequential_range only for true loop-carried dependencies, nl.static_range for small constant loops, nl.fori_loop/nl.while_loop for runtime or data-dependent bounds.
why: affine_range lets the compiler reorder and overlap iterations across engines; sequential_range pins order and blocks pipelining; fori_loop/while_loop are structured on-chip loops that are not unrolled.
trigger: sequential_range used where iterations are independent; dynamic_range or bare while reg: used for runtime loops.
fix: Default to affine_range; reserve sequential_range for carries (cumsum carry, running max); use fori_loop(lower, upper, body) for runtime trip counts.
check_sketch: flag sequential_range loops with no cross-iteration data dependence

rule: Under NKI 0.6.0+ express runtime loops as nl.fori_loop(lower, upper, body_fun, step=1) or nl.while_loop(init, body_fun); for i in nl.dynamic_range(...) and bare while reg: are removed under tracing.
why: The tracer gives a runtime register no value at trace time; fori_loop/while_loop compile on both parser and tracer (tracing default in 0.7.0, parser removed in 0.8.0).
trigger: nl.dynamic_range or while <register>: in kernel code.
fix: def body(i): ...; nl.fori_loop(0, reg, body); or nl.while_loop(reg, body) where body returns the next condition register.
check_sketch: flag nl.dynamic_range and while-loops conditioned on a register

rule: Inside fori_loop/while_loop bodies: keep cross-iteration state in SBUF/HBM mutated in place (no loop-carried Python values), never do raw arithmetic on or write to the loop variable (read it via .ap(scalar_offset=i) or nl.ds), allocate outputs before the loop (PSUM may be inside), use unique op names, and never nest a dynamic loop inside nl.no_reorder().
why: The body is traced once into a separate MLIR region with Pallas-like semantics; the loop variable is a frozen VirtualRegister and tensors created inside are invisible outside.
trigger: Accumulator returned from body, i*TILE computed in Python, output ndarray allocated in body, fori_loop within no_reorder.
fix: Allocate out before the loop; in body use data.ap(scalar_offset=i, indirect_dim=1) or nl.ds(i*T, T); accumulate into an SBUF tile.
check_sketch: lint fori_loop bodies: no new HBM/SBUF outputs used after loop; no Python ops on the index var; not inside no_reorder

rule: Use register instructions (register_alloc(x=...), register_move(dst, src=...), register_load, register_store) only for dynamic loop bounds and while conditions, never for tensor arithmetic; imm= on register_move is removed.
why: Registers drive engine-sequencer branching; tensor math belongs on the vector/scalar engines.

fix: src = nisa.register_alloc(x=10); nisa.register_move(dst=loop_reg, src=src); loop cond via register_store/tensor_scalar/register_load.
check_sketch: flag imm= kwarg on register_move; flag register ops whose result feeds tensor ops

rule: Write a correct single-buffered kernel first, then add double buffering / software pipelining only after a profile shows DMA latency exposed on the critical path.

fix: Allocate 2 (or psum_num_banks) rotating SBUF/PSUM tiles and issue the DMA for tile i+1 before computing tile i; use affine_range so the compiler can overlap.
check_sketch: count MATMULs whose last-finishing dependency is DPA; if > ~10% suggest prefetch/double buffering

rule: Set NEURON_CC_FLAGS --target and NEURON_PLATFORM_TARGET_OVERRIDE to the same platform (trn1/trn1n/inf2/trn2/trn3) and do not pass platform_target= or mode= to @nki.jit.
why: @nki.jit(platform_target=...) and mode= were removed in NKI 0.3.0; the env var is the only override and the compiler auto-detects the framework from arguments.
trigger: @nki.jit(platform_target='trn2') or mismatched env vars.
fix: os.environ['NEURON_CC_FLAGS']='--target trn2 --lnc 1'; os.environ['NEURON_PLATFORM_TARGET_OVERRIDE']='trn2'; plain @nki.jit.
check_sketch: flag jit kwargs platform_target/mode; compare --target to NEURON_PLATFORM_TARGET_OVERRIDE

rule: Pin each concurrent process to its own NeuronCore with NEURON_RT_VISIBLE_CORES and give it a unique NEURON_RT_INSPECT_OUTPUT_DIR.
why: Concurrent agents/processes on shared cores cause device contention, skewed latency and NEFF/NTFF collisions.
trigger: Multiple kernels being compiled/profiled on the same host.
fix: os.environ['NEURON_RT_VISIBLE_CORES']='0'; os.environ['NEURON_RT_INSPECT_OUTPUT_DIR']=f'./output/session-{os.getpid()}'.
check_sketch: harness sets NEURON_RT_VISIBLE_CORES and per-pid output dir

rule: Add --verbose=info (or debug) only when inspecting compiler behaviour; read log-neuron-cc.txt in /tmp/$USER/neuroncc_compile_workdir/<uuid>/ for allocation and optimization decisions.
why: Verbose modes increase compile time; the workdir log is where memory-allocation and pass information appears.
trigger: Unexpected codegen, spills, or performance anomalies.
fix: NEURON_CC_FLAGS='--target trn2 --lnc 1 --verbose=info'; ls -lt /tmp/$USER/neuroncc_compile_workdir/ | head -5.

rule: Import with import nki / nki.isa as nisa / nki.language as nl; importing neuronxcc.nki inside kernels is a compilation error in NKI 0.4.0.
why: The neuronxcc.nki namespace is the Beta-1 path and is no longer accepted (warning in 0.3.0, error in 0.4.0).
trigger: import neuronxcc.nki... in kernel source.
fix: import nki; import nki.isa as nisa; import nki.language as nl (neuronxcc.nki.typing only for nt.tensor annotations).
check_sketch: flag 'import neuronxcc.nki' except neuronxcc.nki.typing

rule: Move data with nisa.dma_copy(dst=..., src=...) only; nl.load / nl.store are removed.
why: Beta-2+ unified HBM<->SBUF movement into the explicit dma_copy ISA call with dst/src access patterns.
trigger: nl.load(tensor[...]) or nl.store(tensor[...], value=x).
fix: nisa.dma_copy(dst=sbuf_tile, src=hbm[0:128, 0:512]); nisa.dma_copy(dst=hbm[0:128, 0:512], src=sbuf_tile).
check_sketch: flag nl.load / nl.store calls

rule: Pass an explicit, pre-allocated dst= tensor to every nisa.* call and never assign its return value.
why: ISA functions write in place into a declared buffer; the result = nisa.func(...) form is Beta-1 and does not compile.
trigger: result = nisa.activation(...) style assignments.
fix: out = nl.ndarray(shape, dtype, buffer=nl.sbuf); nisa.activation(dst=out, data=x, op=nl.exp).
check_sketch: flag nisa.* calls used as expressions or lacking dst kwarg

rule: Index with plain slices (tensor[0:128, 0:512]) or nl.ds(start, size) for runtime offsets; nl.mgrid and nl.arange are removed and have 0 production uses.
why: The slicing/.ap() model replaced index-grid tensors; nl.ds takes (start, size) with a compile-time size.
trigger: nl.mgrid[...], nl.arange(...), or nl.ds(start, end).
fix: tensor[:, nl.ds(offset, TILE)] with TILE a compile-time constant; use min() for the last partial tile.
check_sketch: flag nl.mgrid / nl.arange; check nl.ds second arg is a compile-time constant

rule: Clamp boundary tiles with min() when computing sizes; the mask= parameter on ISA calls is removed.
why: Masks were a Beta-1 mechanism; the compiler now expects exact slice extents.
trigger: mask= kwarg on any nisa call.
fix: f_size = min(F_TILE, total - f_start); operate on tile[0:p, 0:f_size].
check_sketch: flag mask= kwarg

rule: Use nl.maximum / nl.minimum as reduce and elementwise ops and nl.float32 / nl.add (never numpy symbols) inside kernels; drop negate=, reverse0=, dtype= from tensor_reduce.
why: nl.max/nl.min and numpy dtypes/ops are Beta-1 names not recognized by the NKI 0.4.0 frontend.
trigger: nl.max, nl.min, np.float32, np.add, tensor_reduce(..., negate=...).
fix: nisa.tensor_reduce(dst=m, data=x, op=nl.maximum, axis=(1,)).
check_sketch: flag nl.max/nl.min/np.* inside @nki.jit bodies and removed reduce kwargs

rule: Pass buffer objects (nl.sbuf, nl.psum, nl.hbm) not strings, and allocate every kernel output with buffer=nl.shared_hbm.
why: String buffer names and nl.hbm outputs are NKI 0.3.0 removals; shared_hbm marks the tensor as visible to the caller.
trigger: buffer='sbuf' or output nl.ndarray(..., buffer=nl.hbm).
fix: out = nl.ndarray(shape, dtype, buffer=nl.shared_hbm); return out.
check_sketch: flag string buffer args; flag returned tensors whose buffer != shared_hbm

rule: Pass DGE mode as dge_mode=nisa.dge_mode.{none,swdge,hwdge}; integer enum values and engine= are rejected.
why: NKI 0.3.0 replaced integer enum constants with named enums and renamed the parameter.
trigger: dge_mode=2 or engine=nisa.dge.
fix: nisa.dma_copy(dst=d, src=s, dge_mode=nisa.dge_mode.hwdge).
check_sketch: flag integer dge_mode values and engine= kwarg on dma_copy

rule: Express dynamic (runtime) source/destination offsets with tensor.ap(pattern=..., scalar_offset=reg, indirect_dim=d) on nisa.tensor_copy / dma_copy; tensor_copy_dynamic_src/dst are removed and no helper APIs exist.
why: Runtime offsets come from VirtualRegisters or SBUF values and are consumed by the access-pattern generator, not by dedicated copy variants.
trigger: nisa.tensor_copy_dynamic_src(...) / _dynamic_dst(...) or invented helpers.
fix: nisa.tensor_copy(dst=d, src=s.ap(scalar_offset=dyn_offset)); for HBM gathers tensor.ap(pattern=[[512,128],[1,256]], scalar_offset=idx_sb, indirect_dim=0).
check_sketch: flag tensor_copy_dynamic_* identifiers

rule: Declare kernel signatures without a keyword-only '*' separator, with tuple (not list) defaults for collection params, and compare with ==/!= (not is/is not) in kernel conditionals.
why: The NKI frontend parses a restricted Python subset; these forms fail to compile under 0.3.0+.
trigger: def kernel(X, *, flag=True), stride=[1,1], if x is not None.
fix: def kernel(X, flag=True, stride=(1, 1)); if x != None:.
check_sketch: AST lint: no kwonly args, list defaults, or Is/IsNot comparisons in @nki.jit functions

rule: When a dma_copy src and dst have different element types (e.g. uint16 bits holding float4 packs), reinterpret with .view(dtype) so both sides match.
why: DMA moves raw bytes; the compiler rejects mismatched element types under HWDGE unless the view makes them identical.
trigger: nisa.dma_copy(dst=f4_tile, src=ui16_tensor, dge_mode=hwdge).
fix: src=src.view(nl.float4_e2m1fn_x4).
check_sketch: dma_copy: assert src.dtype == dst.dtype (after views)

rule: Pass the axis that matches the actual tensor rank to nisa.tensor_reduce on 3D/4D tiles (reduce innermost first, e.g. axis=2 then axis=1); do not copy Beta-2 axis=1 examples blindly.
why: Beta-2 axis handling was buggy; 0.3.0+ reduces exactly the stated free axis, so a wrong axis silently reduces the wrong dimension.
trigger: tensor_reduce(axis=1) on a (128, 64, 32) tile intended to reduce the last dim.
fix: partial (128,64,1) = reduce(axis=2); final (128,1,1) = reduce(partial, axis=1).
check_sketch: tensor_reduce: assert dst.shape == data.shape with reduced axes set to 1

rule: Call nisa.affine_select(dst, pattern, ch_mul, on_true, on_false, offset=offset) with offset as a keyword, not positionally after pattern.
why: The 0.3.0 signature reordered parameters; positional offset lands in ch_mul.
trigger: affine_select(dst, pattern, offset, ch_mul, ...).
fix: Use the keyword form offset=...
check_sketch: flag affine_select with > 2 positional args before ch_mul

rule: Annotate caller-allocated output tensors with neuronxcc.nki.typing.tensor (nt.tensor) and return None; use nt only for that purpose.
why: Mutable-output kernels write into pre-allocated HBM, avoiding an extra output allocation/copy in the framework; nt is the only sanctioned neuronxcc import.
trigger: Kernel that must write into a framework-owned buffer.
fix: def k(x: nl.ndarray, out: nt.tensor) -> None: nisa.dma_copy(dst=out[...], src=res_sb).
check_sketch: flag neuronxcc imports other than nki.typing

rule: .ap(pattern=[[stride, size], ...], offset=...) strides, sizes and offset must be compile-time constants (in elements, not bytes); only scalar_offset may be a runtime register.
why: Access patterns are baked into descriptors at compile time; runtime variation is limited to the scalar_offset/indirect mechanism.
trigger: Pattern entries computed from a register or data-dependent value.
fix: Hoist pattern computation to Python; use scalar_offset for the runtime part.
check_sketch: ap(): all pattern elements are int literals/compile-time ints

rule: Validate inputs with kernel_assert (emits [NCC_INKI016] Kernel validation exception) instead of bare assert, and compute tile counts with div_ceil.
why: Structured error text makes kernel-origin failures identifiable inside frameworks; div_ceil removes off-by-one remainder bugs.
trigger: assert x.shape[0] <= 128 or (n + d - 1) // d inline.
fix: kernel_assert(cond, msg); num_tiles = div_ceil(n, 128); inline both helpers if nkilib is not installed.
check_sketch: flag bare assert in @nki.jit bodies

rule: Identify the bottleneck as the engine with the largest interval-merged active time among Tensor, Vector, Scalar, GpSimd and DMA; perfect_pipeline equals that time.
why: With perfect overlap the kernel cannot be faster than its busiest engine; the gap total_time -> perfect_pipeline is cross-engine serialization.
trigger: Any profile analysis; Summary.*_engine_active_time and dma_active_time.
fix: engine_times = {Tensor, Vector, Scalar, GpSimd, DMA: memory_bound}; bottleneck = argmax; focus on that family's gaps.
check_sketch: perfect_pipeline = max(engine_active_ns); serialization_gap = total_time - perfect_pipeline

rule: Decompose a DMA-bound kernel into three gaps: DMA idle (total_time - memory_bound), DMA inefficiency (memory_bound - dma_transfer_bytes/peak_bw), and excess traffic ((dma_transfer_bytes - necessary_bytes)/peak_bw).
why: memory_bound is actual DMA wall-clock; memory_bound_ideal is the same bytes at peak bandwidth; memory_bound_ideal_no_reloads moves each IN/OUT tensor exactly once.
trigger: bottleneck == DMA.
fix: Large excess gap -> run redundant-DMA investigation first; large inefficiency gap -> DMA efficiency (descriptor size); idle gap -> do not speculate on cause.
check_sketch: memory_bound = merged DMA ns; ideal = bytes/peak; no_reloads = sum(TensorInfo.size for type in IN,OUT)/peak

numbers.V0_example: DMA inefficiency 59.6% + excess traffic 29.6% of total

rule: Decompose a TE-bound kernel into TE idle (total_time - te_active), TE underutilization (te_active - hw_flops/te_peak), and transpose overhead (transpose_flops/te_peak).
why: compute_bound is interval-merged TE active time; compute_bound_ideal assumes peak FLOP rate; useful_flops excludes TRANSPOSE matmuls.
trigger: bottleneck == Tensor.
fix: Underutilization -> check tile sizes (te_inefficiency); transpose gap -> pre-transpose operands; idle -> check what MATMULs wait on.
check_sketch: compute_bound = merged TE ns; ideal = sum(adjusted_flops)/te_peak; useful = (hw - transpose)/te_peak

rule: Bound the expected gain of any single-engine optimization by bn_speedup = total_time / max(bound_time, slowest non-improved engine time).
why: Removing overhead on one engine only helps until another engine becomes the limiter; e.g. eliminating all DMA overhead in V0 capped speedup at 1.79x because TE was at 4806 us.
trigger: Deciding whether to invest in a memory-side or compute-side fix.
fix: Compute bn_speedup for each candidate bound and pick the family with the largest achievable ratio.
check_sketch: bn_speedup = total_time / max(bound, max_non_impacted_engine_time)

rule: Treat gaps as lower bounds on per-category overhead, not predicted savings; re-profile and recompute bounds after each change because the bottleneck engine and gap structure shift.
why: Gaps assume peak bandwidth/throughput, the engine may not be on the critical path, and engine times are coupled (data-starved TE active time shrinks when DMA improves).
trigger: After any optimization step.
fix: Profile again with the same methodology, present side-by-side bounds, and pick the next investigation from the new bottleneck.
check_sketch: store bounds per iteration; diff them

rule: Compute excess_ratio = dma_transfer_bytes / necessary_bytes and split the excess into input reloads (IN tensors with repeat > 1) versus spills ([VIRTUAL] transfers) before choosing a fix.
why: Reloads are fixed by blocking/reuse; spills by shrinking live SBUF; they need different code changes.
trigger: memory_bound_ideal -> memory_bound_ideal_no_reloads gap is large.
fix: Per-tensor repeat = transferred/size; flag IN tensors with repeat > 1.5; spill_bytes from [VIRTUAL] rows; localize via Instruction -> Flow -> DmaPacketAggregated filtered to source == '[[INPUT]]'.
check_sketch: excess_ratio > 1.0; reload_excess = sum(total - size for IN repeat > 1); spill = VIRTUAL bytes

rule: When both the excess-traffic and DMA-inefficiency gaps are large, fix reloads first; the excess traffic is itself made of inefficient transfers.
why: Excess inefficient loads inflate both gaps; removing the reloads removes a proportional share of the inefficiency gap for free.
trigger: excess gap proportionally large alongside inefficiency gap.
fix: Block/reuse to cut reloads, re-profile, then widen transfers.
check_sketch: if excess_gap/memory_bound > ~0.25 and inefficiency_gap large -> prioritize reloads

rule: If the DMA efficiency gap (memory_bound - memory_bound_ideal) is under ~5% of memory_bound, stop optimizing transfer sizes and look at excess traffic or other engines.
why: Peak bandwidth is never fully achievable; a small residual gap is per-transfer overhead that cannot be removed.
trigger: Memory-bound kernel after transfer-widening.
fix: Switch to redundant-DMA or pipelining investigations.
check_sketch: efficiency_gap / memory_bound < 0.05 -> transfers efficient

rule: Attribute DMA to source lines using Instruction rows with hbm_read_bytes > 0 (loads) or hbm_write_bytes > 0 (stores) joined via Flow to DmaPacketAggregated, and report shape = partitions x (transfer_bytes / partitions).
why: hbm_read/write_bytes are populated regardless of DGE mode/engine; descriptor size per partition is what governs DMA throughput.
trigger: Localizing DMA inefficiency.
fix: Group by bir_debug_info_source_location; sort by bytes; flag desc_bytes < 4096; note DPA coverage may be < 100% for swdge transfers.
check_sketch: desc_bytes = median(transfer_bytes)/median(write_num_sbuf_partitions or read_num_sbuf_partitions)

rule: Measure TE utilization as sum(adjusted_flops)/te_active_ns against te_peak, and extract K, M, N per MATMUL source line from Instruction.operands (trailing 'K*M', N from src stride) to find undersized tiles.
why: Utilization below ~90% with full tiles indicates throttling/idle-induced inflation; below that with K or M < 128 indicates tile-size loss.
trigger: compute_bound -> compute_bound_ideal_flops gap is large.
fix: Re-tile lines with K<128 or M<128; verify the user is not doing intentional PE tiling first.

rule: Classify each MATMUL's last-finishing dependency (previous MATMUL = normal pipeline, DPA = DMA-starved, Vector = PSUM evacuation) to decide between prefetching and compute fixes.
why: In a healthy pipeline ~95% of MATMULs wait only on the previous MATMUL; a high DPA share means the DMA schedule, not TE, limits throughput.
trigger: TE idle gap or TE underutilization gap present.
fix: If DPA-gated share is high: enlarge/prefetch loads (row loads, double buffering); if Vector-gated: speed up PSUM->SBUF copies.
check_sketch: count MATMUL rows by last-finishing dependency engine; DMA-gated fraction > ~10% -> memory-side fix

rule: Expect TE active time to be inflated by throttling/warm-up after idle gaps and by late-arriving weights; fix the DMA side before concluding TE is inefficient.
why: Individual MATMUL durations lengthen when data is late, so compute-family bounds computed from current TE active time overstate remaining compute overhead.
trigger: TE underutilization gap with full-size tiles.
fix: Reduce DMA idle/starvation first (V1 -> V2: TE underutil fell from 416 to 33 us without touching matmul code).
check_sketch: if tiles are full and utilization < 90%, check DMA-gated MATMUL fraction before re-tiling

rule: When perfect_pipeline exceeds both memory_bound and compute_bound (Vector/Scalar/GpSimd is the bottleneck), section the kernel logically and run windowed bounds per phase instead of whole-kernel analysis.
why: These engines play diverse roles, so there is no single 'ideal' bound; windowing [t0,t1] over the raw tables isolates which phase overloads them.
trigger: Vector/Scalar/GpSimd active time is the arg-max.
fix: Recompute input quantities from DmaPacket/ActiveTime/Instruction clipped to each window; attribute instructions by bir_debug_info_source_location and duration.
check_sketch: per window: engine_active_ns per engine; rank source lines by SUM(duration_ns) per engine

rule: Decide whether a kernel is memory- or compute-bound by comparing mm_arithmetic_intensity (FLOPs per DMA byte) with peak_flops_bandwidth_ratio, and by comparing necessary_bytes/peak_bw with hw_flops/te_peak before optimizing.
why: The larger of the two ideal bounds is the true floor; a batch=1 decode matmul has intensity ~2 FLOP/byte, far below trn2's ~180 FLOP/byte break-even, so it is DMA-bound regardless of TE tuning.
trigger: Planning an optimization for a new kernel.
fix: jq '{intensity: .mm_arithmetic_intensity, peak_ratio: .peak_flops_bandwidth_ratio}'; if intensity << ratio, spend effort on DMA (contiguity, descriptor size, reloads), not tiles.
check_sketch: intensity = hw_flops / dma_transfer_bytes; compare to te_peak / dma_bw_peak

fix: neuron-explorer capture -n $NEFF -s profile.ntff --profile-nth-exec=2 --enable-dge-notifs; check DmaPacket COUNT(*) > 0 before analysis.
check_sketch: assert DmaPacket count > 0 and Instruction.bir_debug_info_source_location not all NULL

rule: When source-level DMA attribution matters, compile the profiled variant with dge_mode none or hwdge; DmaPacketAggregated and Instruction->DPA flow links may be missing for swdge (or compiler-chosen 'unknown').
why: Depending on NKI/neuronx-cc version the aggregated packet table is only produced for hwdge/none transfers, so reload/spill localization and descriptor-size analysis skip swdge lines.
trigger: DPA coverage < 95% of dma_transfer_bytes.
fix: Temporarily switch dge_mode=nisa.dge_mode.hwdge for the profiling run, or accept Step-1 totals only.
check_sketch: coverage = sum(DPA.transfer_bytes)/dma_transfer_bytes; warn if < 0.95

rule: Apply fillna(0) to Summary.transpose_flops before comparing; it is NaN for kernels with no transposes.
why: The summary field is undefined rather than zero when no TRANSPOSE matmuls exist.
trigger: Reading Summary.transpose_flops.
fix: summary['transpose_flops'] = summary['transpose_flops'].fillna(0).
check_sketch: treat NaN transpose_flops as 0

rule: Generate inputs and references on CPU, not on the XLA device, when profiling; on-device torch ops compile into extra NEFFs or get fused into the kernel's execution and obfuscate its profile.
why: Each XLA graph is a separate NEFF; device-side random generation can be fused with the kernel launch.
trigger: Multiple NEFFs in NEURON_RT_INSPECT_OUTPUT_DIR; identify-neffs.py shows [XLA:...] entries.
fix: x = torch.randn(...).to(device) only for kernel inputs; everything else on CPU; use identify-neffs.py to pick the [NKI:<func>] NEFF.
check_sketch: flag torch ops on xla tensors in the harness other than the kernel call

rule: Map ops to engines deliberately: nc_matmul and nc_transpose on TensorE (PSUM output), activation/reciprocal/rsqrt (with fused scale/bias) on ScalarE, tensor_tensor/tensor_scalar/tensor_reduce/tensor_tensor_scan/bn_stats on VectorE, dma_copy/dma_transpose/dma_compute on the 16 DMA queues, stream shuffle / collectives on GpSimd paths.
why: Each engine has its own instruction stream; balancing work across TensorE, VectorE, ScalarE, GpSimd and DMA is what lets the compiler overlap them (perfect_pipeline = max engine time).
trigger: One engine's active time dominates while others are idle (e.g. all elementwise work on VectorE while ScalarE is at 0%).
fix: Move elementwise unary math to nisa.activation (ScalarE) and binary/reduction work to VectorE so the two run concurrently; keep PSUM evacuation (tensor_copy) off the busiest engine.

rule: Do all gather/strided/reordered indexing on the HBM side of a DMA (any dim, any stride, N-D) and keep SBUF-side access contiguous.
why: HBM has no partition structure and DMA descriptors can express arbitrary strides, whereas SBUF dim 0 is physically partitioned.
trigger: Attempting strided or permuted access on an SBUF tensor to match an HBM layout.
fix: Put the TensorView/.ap() with strides on the HBM operand of dma_copy and write a dense [P, F] SBUF tile.
check_sketch: dma_copy: SBUF-side pattern innermost stride == 1 while HBM side may be strided

rule: Expect strided DMA to be functional on gen2 but only optimized on gen3+ (trn2/trn3); budget extra time for strided loads on trn1/inf2.
why: gen3 added optimized strided DMA paths; gen2 has basic support only.
trigger: Strided TensorView DMA on --target trn1/inf2 running slower than expected.
fix: On gen2 prefer layout changes or contiguous loads with on-chip relayout for small tensors.

rule: Select features by generation: gen2 (trn1/inf2) baseline; gen3 (trn2) adds FP8 and Double-FP8 mode; gen4 (trn3) adds MXFP8/MXFP4 Quad-MX mode, PSUM free dim up to 4096 fp32 / 8192 bf16, LNC up to 8, and .indirect() on compute ops.
why: Kernels that assume gen4 limits or dtypes fail or under-tile on older targets and vice versa.
trigger: Hardcoded generation-specific constants or dtypes without a target check.
fix: Derive limits from the documented table for the --target in use; gate FP8/MX/indirect paths on generation.
check_sketch: map --target to generation and validate dtypes/limits against the feature table

rule: Load small per-kernel parameters (bias, scale, gamma) once outside the tile loops and reuse the SBUF copy.
why: Reloading a parameter per tile multiplies small inefficient DMAs and adds reload traffic.
trigger: dma_copy of a [H] parameter inside the sequence/batch tile loop.
fix: Move the parameter dma_copy before the loops (or once per outer tile if SBUF-constrained) and broadcast via a view.
check_sketch: flag dma_copy whose src is loop-invariant inside an unrolled loop

rule: Tile large matmul N to the PSUM free limit and copy each PSUM tile to SBUF immediately after its accumulation group completes to free the bank.
why: PSUM capacity is small (banks of 512 fp32 per partition on gen2/3); holding results delays subsequent matmuls that need the bank.
trigger: nc_matmul loops that keep many PSUM results live or allocate PSUM larger than the limit.
fix: for f in range(0, N, 512): psum=(M,512); matmul; tensor_copy(dst=sb[:, f:f+512], src=psum).
check_sketch: track live PSUM tiles per loop body; flag > psum_num_banks or PSUM shape[1] > limit

rule: Apply post-matmul epilogues (gelu, bias, scaling, quantization) directly on the PSUM->SBUF result before the single HBM store.
why: Epilogue fusion avoids a write and a read of the full activation at HBM bandwidth.
trigger: dma_copy(dst=hbm_temp, src=result) followed by reload for the epilogue.
fix: tensor_copy(psum->sbuf); nisa.activation(dst=sb, data=sb, op=nl.gelu); dma_copy(dst=out, src=sb).
check_sketch: flag HBM temp written from matmul result and read back in the same kernel

rule: Issue independent nc_transpose (or matmul) groups into distinct PSUM banks so they can execute concurrently rather than serializing on one bank.
why: The tensor engine can pipeline into separate PSUM banks; sharing a bank forces a wait for the evacuation of the previous result.
trigger: Loop of transposes all targeting the same PSUM tile.
fix: Allocate psum_bank_0 / psum_bank_1 with address=(0, i*2048) and alternate per iteration.

rule: Use stride-0 (.broadcast / .ap stride 0) only on free dims or a size-1 partition dim; cross-partition replication of a non-size-1 partition needs stream_shuffle_broadcast or a matmul.
why: TensorView.broadcast(dim=0, size=128) is allowed only if the original partition size is 1; otherwise data must physically move between partitions.
trigger: Broadcasting a [k, F] (k>1) tile across partitions by view.
fix: Load the vector into partition 0 and call stream_shuffle_broadcast, or compute ones[128,1] @ row via nc_matmul.
check_sketch: broadcast(dim=0) requires shape[0] == 1
